sasha: quick sync — I'm seeing inconsistent abort semantics between the node and go SDKs when a stream is cancelled mid-response. Node abort leaves a partial final token and the client gets a truncated chunk; Go returns io.EOF and the stream appears 'completed'. anyone else run into this?

lucas: yep noticed that last week. i think it's the difference between how we cancel the http request vs how the runtime flushes the socket. Node's AbortController aborts the fetch which can cut the http body mid-chunk. Go's context cancel often lets the underlying net/http finish the current read and then returns EOF. :thinking:

vivian: can you paste minimal repros? node and go versions? also which transport (fetch/axios for node)?

sasha: repros below. node:
```js
const ac = new AbortController();
const r = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', body, signal: ac.signal });
// start reading r.body as stream, then ac.abort() while last token is being streamed
```

go repro:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", url, bytes.NewReader(body))
resp, _ := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
// read resp.Body, call cancel() mid-read
```
Observed: node stream handler gets a chunk missing final bytes and throws, go's reader returns nil, io.EOF.

raj: fwiw the server runtime emits a terminal event ("event: done") when generation completes. if the transport is cut earlier we'd see partial content. maybe node abort is closing the socket immediately and not waiting for the runtime to send done.

lucas: proposed SDK side fixes: 1) change node SDK to call abort only after signally the application-level stream handler that cancellation is requested, and let underlying ReadableStream end gracefully if possible. 2) document that abort can produce partial tokens and recommend application-level idempotency for streaming partials.

vivian: alternatively we could implement a small client-side draining window: when abort is requested, attempt to read up to N more bytes or until a short timeout (e.g., 200ms) before force-closing. that buys time for the runtime to finish last chunk. might be surprising for very low-latency SLOs though.

ci-bot: deploy queued: /rollout sdk-node@canary  — will run smoke tests including streaming-cancel tests.

sasha: lucas — can you draft a tiny change for node SDK that does a graceful drain with a configurable timeout? add explicit tests that simulate runtime sending final event with small delay. i'll pair on the go side to make sure semantics are consistent.

lucas: yep i'll open a PR, tests + changelog. thinking config name `gracefulAbortTimeoutMs` default 0 (off) to avoid changing behavior, set to 200ms when teams opt-in.

vivian: we should also add a spec entry: table of expected outcomes when cancel happens at various points (before first token, mid-token, after done). helps app teams understand guarantees.

raj: +1. also callout retriable vs non-retriable scenarios: if abort happens mid-token you can't really retry without risk of duplication unless server supports idempotent partials. include recommended server-side markers.

sasha: ok next steps: lucas PR for node with opt-in drain; sasha/vivian pair on spec doc; raj to add server-side marker proposal; i'll schedule follow-up async review by EOD tomorrow. ping me if you want to pair earlier. :thumbsup:

lucas: assigning self to PR and test work. thanks.

vivian: i'll stub the spec in /docs/streaming-cancel.md and drop a link here when ready.

sasha: thanks all. short note: if anyone owns mobile SDKs (objc/swift/kotlin) pls check how their cancel maps to underlying transport — might hit same partial-token issue.

lucas: noted, i'll mention in PR and add a test matrix.

raj: filing a runtime issue to see if we can emit an OS-level FIN after terminal event faster to reduce race window.

sasha: great. end of thread.
